instruction: Solve blind from the stimulus below only. Do not open the question file or any file containing model answers. Answer parts a, b, c in your own words, then give a verdict per part.
stimulus: Secondary passage written for this question. Before Europeans arrived, Native peoples across North America had built many different ways of life. In the Southeast and Midwest, Mississippian chiefdoms farmed maize in river valleys and raised great earthen mounds at Cahokia. In the arid Southwest, Pueblo peoples farmed dry land and built adobe villages. In the Northeast woodlands, Iroquois villagers farmed maize, beans, and squash together. On the rainy Pacific coast, peoples fished for salmon and built settled villages without farming maize.

parts.prompt: Identify one way in which environment shaped how a Native society in the passage lived.
Explain how maize farming helped Mississippian chiefdoms like Cahokia grow large.
Explain one similarity between the Pueblo peoples and the Iroquois villagers described in the passage.
